subject.name_or_desc: A person of honour asked Lilly

context.question: If his Excellency Robert Earl of Essex should take Reading, having then surrounded it with his army?
context.asked_at: During the siege of Reading (the town was delivered 27 April; the year is printed '1644' in the 1647 OCR but the historical siege of Reading ended in April 1643 — see notes)
context.setting: Robert, Earl of Essex, Parliament's general, had surrounded Reading with his army; the town was held for the King, governor Sir Arthur Aston (spelled 'Acton' in the 1852 edition)

attachments.key_positions: Mars, lord of Scorpio (the sign ascending per the 1852 judgment), significator of Essex, well fortified except being in his fall, and in reception with the Moon (Mars in her house, she in his terms and face, near Regulus, in the 10th); Moon void of course, applying to a sextile of Mars (equivalent to a square in signs of long ascension); Sun, the King's significator, in the 7th in a fixed sign; Aquarius, the sign on the 4th, for the town; Saturn lord of the 4th for the governor, in his fall; Jupiter lord of the 5th and Venus placed therein for the town's ammunition and provision
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment (Chap. LXVI in the 1647 printing; Fig. 21 in the 1852 edition).

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
